summary: Goochland County, Virginia, tower listed as standing at Rassawek and relocated from East Leake; no dates given, and the name matches a Fluvanna archaeological site.

events.note: Listed as relocated from East Leake; the list gives no date or reason
East Leake (Loc 1) and East Leake (Gum Spring) listed as gone; the list gives no dates

evidence.supports: Rassawek listed as relocated from East Leake and standing
Rassawek listed as relocated from East Leake, Goochland, standing
East Leake (Gum Spring) listed as gone
Rassawek is an archaeological site in Fluvanna County
evidence.quote: Rassawek is an archaeological site in Fluvanna County, Virginia

evidence.supports: location at the confluence of the James and Rivanna rivers
evidence.quote: located at the confluence of the James River and its tributary

evidence.supports: former village serving as the Monacan capital
evidence.quote: The site was previously a village that served as the capital for the Monacans

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Rassawek is also the name of an archaeological site in Fluvanna County (Wikipedia). The Forest Fire Lookout Association places this tower in Goochland County and does not explain the name. The distance of about 3.8 km between the listed point and the Wikipedia coordinates is computed.
Two East Leake points are listed as gone. The list does not say which one the Rassawek tower came from.

notes_for_editor: Only the two FFLA Virginia lists and Wikipedia's Rassawek page were read; two web searches on the East Leake move found no dated or sourced account. The record us-va-east-leake-loc-1 says the Loc 1 tower was moved to Rassawek, but the FFLA list does not name which East Leake point Rassawek came from. That claim is unverified. Search snippets mentioning an older listing for East Leake (South Anna, VDOF, removed) were not fetched and are not used. Distance of about 16.5 km between East Leake (Loc 1) and the Rassawek point is computed from the listed coordinates. The name Rassawek belongs to a sensitive Monacan archaeological site; the story reports only what the sources state.
